newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish 10-yr bond price slips ahead of T-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Danish 10-yr bond price slips ahead of T-bill sale.

text.p: True to expectations, the Danish benchmark bond was virtually becalmed on Monday, with players choosing to wait for Tuesday's four percent T-bill auction and U.S. data due later in the week.
"There are not really any net buyers or sellers," a dealer said.
At 1230 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down from its opening 109.16, to 109.10, yielding 6.63 percent in modest turnover of around 700 million crowns.
Its March future, however, rose 0.12 point to 108.32, with 155 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.23 point to 86.28.
The crown traded at 3.8187 per mark, firming from its earlier 3.8201. --Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969659
